data.title: Balance Scale Meanings
data.description: Answer the tutor out loud to explain what the equal sign means using balance scales.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are balanced.
items.ask: Three plus two equals five. When we look at this on a balance scale, what does the equal sign mean?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that state the two sides match, are even, or hold the same weight count as correct.
items.signatureError: Saying the sum, five, is NOT an explanation of the equal sign.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are balanced, just like three plus two has the same weight as five.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are balanced.
items.ask: Four equals two plus two. What does the equal sign tell us about these two sides?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that explain that both sides match or are the same count.
items.signatureError: Saying that the answer comes next or just reading the numbers is NOT correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are balanced, showing that four is the same amount as two plus two.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are balanced.
items.ask: One plus four equals three plus two. Tell us what the equal sign shows on a balance scale.
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing that says the two sides are equal, even, or match counts.
items.signatureError: Saying the total number five is NOT an explanation of the equal sign.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are balanced, so one plus four has the exact same value as three plus two.

data.title: Pattern Rules
data.description: You will answer out loud to explain the secret rules behind patterns.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding two each time.
items.ask: Look at these numbers: two, four, six, eight. What is the rule of this pattern?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing that correctly names skipping by twos or adding two counts as the right answer.
items.signatureError: Saying the next number in the pattern, like ten, is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The rule is plus two because every number goes up by two. We say plus two.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern repeats red and blue in order.
items.ask: Look at the colors: red, blue, red, blue. What is the secret rule of this pattern?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words describing the alternating color sequence count as the answer.
items.signatureError: Naming just one color like red is NOT the rule of the pattern.
items.correctionBody: The pattern alternates between red and blue. The rule is red then blue.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding five each time.
items.ask: Look at this sequence: five, ten, fifteen, twenty. What rule makes this pattern grow?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any description of counting up by fives or adding five counts as the answer.
items.signatureError: Saying the last number twenty is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The numbers grow by five each time, so the rule is plus five.
